content.directions: Suppose you are asked to give advice on whether to major in science or humanities at college, write an essay to state your opinion. You are required to write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
content.topic: Whether to major in science or humanities at college

modelEssay.title: Whether to Major in Science or Humanities at College
modelEssay.content:
When it comes to choosing a major in college, the debate between science and humanities has been a long-standing one. Personally, I believe that the choice should be based on individual interests and career goals.

Firstly, science majors often lead to careers with high demand and lucrative salaries. The fields of technology, engineering, and medicine are constantly evolving and require skilled professionals. Moreover, a background in science equips students with analytical skills that are valuable in any profession.

On the other hand, humanities majors cultivate critical thinking and a broad understanding of society and culture. They prepare students for careers in law, education, and the arts, which are equally important for societal development. Additionally, the skills gained from humanities, such as communication and empathy, are indispensable in today's globalized world.

In conclusion, the decision to major in science or humanities should not be made lightly. It is crucial to consider personal passion and the type of impact one wishes to make in the future. Both fields are essential and offer unique opportunities for personal and professional growth.

structureAnalysis.paragraph1: 引入段：提出选择专业的问题，表达个人观点，即选择应基于个人兴趣和职业目标
structureAnalysis.paragraph2: 展开段：分别论述科学专业的优势（职业需求和薪酬）和人文学科的价值（批判性思维和文化理解）
structureAnalysis.paragraph3: 总结段：强调选择专业的重要性，重申个人兴趣和未来影响的重要性，并总结两个领域的重要性

highlights: 使用了'when it comes to'等高级表达引入话题
运用了'Firstly...On the other hand...'等结构清晰地对比两个专业
逻辑清晰，过渡自然（Moreover, Additionally, In conclusion）
词汇丰富，避免重复（majors, fields, careers, professionals, skills）

transcript.text: Conversation 1.
transcript.translation: 对话一。

transcript.text: Mr. Ishiguro, have you ever found one of your books at a second-hand bookstore?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 石黑先生，您曾经在二手书店里发现过自己的书吗？

transcript.text: Yes, that kind of thing is difficult. If they've got my book there, I think, well, this is an insult. Somebody didn't want to keep my book. But if it's not there, I feel it's an insult too. I think, why aren't people exchanging my book? Why isn't it in this store?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 有过，那种事让人很为难。如果店里摆着我的书，我会想，唉，这是一种侮辱，有人不想留着我的书。可如果店里没有我的书，我也觉得是一种侮辱。我会想，为什么大家不转卖我的书？为什么这家店里没有它？

transcript.text: Does being a writer require a thick skin?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 当作家是不是需要脸皮厚一点？

transcript.text: Yes. For example, my wife can be very harsh. I began working on my latest book, The Buried Giant, in 2004. But I stopped after I showed my wife a little section. She thought it was rubbish.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 是的。比如说，我妻子可以非常严厉。我从2004年开始写我最新的书《被掩埋的巨人》，但在把一小段拿给妻子看之后我就停笔了。她觉得那是垃圾。

transcript.text: Even after you won a Booker Prize?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 即便您已经拿过布克奖了吗？

transcript.text: She's not intimidated at all. And she criticizes me in exactly the same way she did when I was first unpublished and I was starting out.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 她一点也不被吓住。她批评我的方式，跟我当年还没出版、刚起步时一模一样。

transcript.text: But you would never compromise on your vision.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 但您绝不会在自己的创作理念上妥协吧。

transcript.text: No, I wouldn't ever compromise on the essential — the ideas or the themes. This isn't really what my wife is trying to criticize me about. It's always about execution.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 不会，我绝不会在最核心的东西上妥协——也就是思想或主题。我妻子真正批评的并不是这些，她针对的始终是执行和写法。

transcript.text: So why did you put your book, The Buried Giant, aside for so long? Apparently you started working on it over ten years ago.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 那您为什么把《被掩埋的巨人》搁置了这么久？据说您十多年前就开始写它了。

transcript.text: I've often stopped writing a book and left it for a few years. And by the time I come back to it, it may have changed. Usually my imagination has moved on and I can think of different contexts or a different way to do it.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我经常会中途停下一本书，把它搁置好几年。等我再回过头来写时，它可能已经变了样。通常我的想象力已经发展到别处，我能想到不同的背景设定或不同的写法。

transcript.text: What does it feel like when you finally finish a book?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 当您终于写完一本书时，那是什么感觉？

transcript.text: It's funny you ask that, because I never have this moment when I feel, ah, I've finished. I watch footballers at the end of the match, you know, the whistle goes and they've won or lost. Until then, they've been giving everything they have, and at that moment they know it's over. It's funny for an author — there's never a finishing whistle.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你问得真有意思，因为我从来没有那种“啊，我写完了”的时刻。我看足球运动员在比赛结束时，哨声一响，他们要么赢要么输。在那之前，他们倾尽全力，而那一刻他们知道一切都结束了。对作家来说很有意思——根本没有一声终场哨。

options.label: C

transcript.text: Conversation 2.
transcript.translation: 对话二。

transcript.text: According to a study of race and equity in education, black athletes are dropping out of college across the country at alarming rates. With us to talk about the findings in this study is Washington Post columnist Kevin Blackstone. Good morning.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 根据一项关于教育中种族与公平的研究，全国各地的黑人运动员正以惊人的速度从大学辍学。今天来和我们谈谈这项研究发现的是《华盛顿邮报》专栏作家凯文·布莱克斯通。早上好。

transcript.text: Good morning. How are you?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 早上好。你好吗？

transcript.text: Fine, thank you. What is new that you found in this study?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 很好，谢谢。这项研究中你发现了什么新内容？

transcript.text: Well, this is Shaun Harper's study, and he points out that on major college campuses across the country, black males make up less than 3% of undergraduate enrollments. Yet, when you look at their numbers or percentages on the revenue-generating sports teams of football and basketball, they make up well into 50 to 60% of those teams. So the idea is that they are really there to be part of the revenue-generating working class of athletes on campus, and not necessarily there to be part of the educating class, as most students in other groups are.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 嗯，这是肖恩·哈珀的研究，他指出，在全国各大高校校园里，黑人男性占本科生入学人数的比例不到3%。然而，当你看他们在橄榄球和篮球这些创收运动队中的人数或比例时，他们却占到了这些球队的50%到60%。所以这意味着，他们在校园里其实是作为创收的运动员劳动阶层而存在的，而不像其他群体的大多数学生那样，是受教育阶层的一部分。

transcript.text: Compared with other groups, I think the numbers in this group at those 65 schools are something like just barely more than half of the black male athletes graduate at all.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 与其他群体相比，我想在那65所学校里，这个群体的数据大概是，仅仅只有刚刚过半的黑人男性运动员能够最终毕业。

transcript.text: Exactly. And what's really bad about this is these athletes are supposedly promised at least one thing as reward for all their blood and sweat, and that is a college degree, which can be a transformative tool in our society when you talk about upward mobility. And that's really the troubling part about this.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 完全正确。而真正糟糕的是，这些运动员据说至少被许诺了一样东西作为他们付出血汗的回报，那就是大学学位。当我们谈到向上的社会流动时，大学学位可以是社会中一种能改变命运的工具。而这正是这件事真正令人担忧的地方。

transcript.text: Well, this has been talked about so much, really, in recent years. Why hasn't it changed?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 嗯，近年来人们其实已经谈论这个问题很多了。为什么它一直没有改变呢？

transcript.text: Well, I think one of the reasons it hasn't changed is because there's really no economic pressure to change this. All of the incentive is really on winning and not losing on the field or on the court. Coaches do not necessarily have the incentive to graduate players.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 嗯，我认为它一直没有改变的原因之一，是确实没有经济上的压力去改变它。所有的激励其实都在于在球场上取胜而不是输球。教练们未必有让球员毕业的动力。

questions.keySentence: I think the numbers in this group at those 65 schools are something like just barely more than half of the black male athletes graduate at all.

options.label: A

options.label: B

options.label: C

questions.analysis: 被问及为何没有改变时，男士说 'Coaches do not necessarily have the incentive to graduate players'，因为激励全在赢球而非育人，故选 A。B、C 把责任推给运动员，与原文相反；D 学校不重视虽相关，但男士明确归因于教练缺乏让球员毕业的动力。

transcript.text: Passage 1.
transcript.translation: 第一篇短文。

transcript.text: America's holiday shopping season starts on Black Friday, the day after Thanksgiving.
transcript.translation: 美国的假日购物季从黑色星期五开始，也就是感恩节后的第二天。

transcript.text: It is the busiest shopping day of the year.
transcript.translation: 这是一年中最繁忙的购物日。

transcript.text: Retailers make the most money this time of year, about 20 to 30 percent of annual revenue.
transcript.translation: 零售商在一年中的这个时候赚钱最多，约占其年收入的百分之二十到三十。

transcript.text: About 136 million people will shop during the Thanksgiving holiday weekend.
transcript.translation: 约有一亿三千六百万人会在感恩节假期周末购物。

transcript.text: More and more will shop online.
transcript.translation: 越来越多的人将在网上购物。

transcript.text: In an era of instant information, shoppers can use their mobile phones to find deals.
transcript.translation: 在这个信息即时获取的时代，购物者可以用手机寻找优惠。

transcript.text: About 183.8 million people will shop on Cyber Monday, the first Monday after Thanksgiving.
transcript.translation: 约有一亿八千三百八十万人将在网络星期一购物，也就是感恩节后的第一个星期一。

transcript.text: More than half of all holiday purchases will be made online.
transcript.translation: 超过一半的假日购物将在网上完成。

transcript.text: One in five Americans will use a tablet or smartphone.
transcript.translation: 五分之一的美国人将使用平板电脑或智能手机购物。

transcript.text: Online spending on Black Friday will rise 15 percent to hit 2.7 billion dollars this year.
transcript.translation: 今年黑色星期五的网上消费将增长百分之十五，达到二十七亿美元。

transcript.text: Cyber Monday spending will increase 12 percent to 3 billion dollars.
transcript.translation: 网络星期一的消费将增长百分之十二，达到三十亿美元。

transcript.text: For many, shopping online was a more comfortable alternative than crowded malls.
transcript.translation: 对许多人来说，网上购物是比拥挤的商场更舒适的选择。

transcript.text: The shift to online shopping has had a big impact on traditional shopping malls.
transcript.translation: 向网上购物的转变对传统购物中心产生了巨大影响。

transcript.text: Since 2010, more than 24 shopping malls have closed and an additional 60 are struggling.
transcript.translation: 自2010年以来，已有超过24家购物中心关闭，另有60家正在苦苦支撑。

transcript.text: However, Fortune says the weakest of the malls have closed; the sector is thriving again.
transcript.translation: 然而，《财富》杂志称，那些最弱的商场已经关闭，这个行业正再次繁荣起来。

transcript.text: The International Council of Shopping Centers said 94.2 percent of malls were full or occupied with shops by the end of 2014.
transcript.translation: 国际购物中心协会表示，到2014年底，百分之九十四点二的购物中心已客满或被店铺占用。

transcript.text: That is the highest level in 27 years.
transcript.translation: 这是27年来的最高水平。

transcript.text: Economist Gus Faucher said lower unemployment and rising wages could give Americans more money to spend.
transcript.translation: 经济学家古斯·福彻表示，失业率下降和工资上涨可能让美国人有更多的钱用于消费。

transcript.text: The average American consumer will spend about 805 dollars on gifts.
transcript.translation: 美国消费者平均将在礼物上花费约805美元。

transcript.text: That's about 630.5 billion dollars between November and December, an increase of 3.7 percent from last year.
transcript.translation: 也就是11月到12月之间约六千三百零五亿美元，比去年增长百分之三点七。

transcript.text: Passage 2.
transcript.translation: 第二篇短文。

transcript.text: For years, many of us have relied on antibiotic use to treat various infections.
transcript.translation: 多年来，我们当中许多人都依赖使用抗生素来治疗各种感染。

transcript.text: And the reality is that antibiotics have been responsible for saving millions of lives since penicillin, one of the earliest antibiotics, was first used on a clinical basis 70 years ago.
transcript.translation: 事实上，自从最早的抗生素之一青霉素在70年前首次用于临床以来，抗生素已经挽救了数百万人的生命。

transcript.text: However, today is a new era in which taking antibiotics can cause some very dangerous and potentially life-threatening situations.
transcript.translation: 然而，如今进入了一个新时代，服用抗生素可能会带来一些非常危险、甚至可能危及生命的情况。

transcript.text: In fact, you may have heard about the new superbugs, which are antibiotic-resistant bacteria that have developed as a result of overprescribed antibiotics.
transcript.translation: 事实上，你可能听说过新出现的超级细菌，它们是由于抗生素被过度开处方而产生的耐抗生素细菌。

transcript.text: In the past, health experts warned us that the day would come in which it would become very difficult to provide medical care for even common problems, such as lung infection or severe sore throat.
transcript.translation: 过去，健康专家曾警告我们，总有一天，即使是肺部感染或严重咽喉痛这样常见的问题，提供医疗救治也会变得非常困难。

transcript.text: And apparently that day has come, because seemingly routine operations such as knee replacements are now much more hazardous due to the looming threat of these infections.
transcript.translation: 显然那一天已经到来，因为像膝关节置换这样看似常规的手术，如今因为这些感染日益逼近的威胁而变得危险得多。

transcript.text: The problem has grown into such epidemic proportions that this severe strain of resistant bacteria is being blamed for nearly 700,000 deaths each year throughout the world.
transcript.translation: 这一问题已经发展到流行病般的规模，以至于这种严重的耐药菌株被认为造成了全世界每年近70万人死亡。

transcript.text: And unfortunately, health experts worry that the number will rise to 10 million or more on a yearly basis by 2050.
transcript.translation: 不幸的是，健康专家担心，到2050年这一数字将每年上升到1000万或更多。

transcript.text: With such a large life-threatening epidemic, it is sad to say that only 1.2% of budgetary money for the National Institutes of Health is currently being spent on research to tackle this problem.
transcript.translation: 面对如此巨大的、危及生命的流行病，可悲的是，目前美国国家卫生研究院仅有1.2%的预算资金被用于解决这一问题的研究。

transcript.text: This is a far cry from the funds necessary for a problem of such magnitude.
transcript.translation: 这与如此严重的问题所需要的资金相差甚远。

transcript.text: Recording 1.
transcript.translation: 录音一。

transcript.text: This is the reason you are here in a university. You are here to be educated. You are here to understand thinking better and to think better yourself.
transcript.translation: 这就是你们身处大学的理由。你们来这里是为了接受教育，来这里是为了更好地理解思考，并让自己思考得更好。

transcript.text: It's not a chance you're going to have throughout your lifetime. For the next few years, you have a chance to focus on thinking.
transcript.translation: 这不是你一生中随时都能拥有的机会。在接下来的几年里，你们有机会专注于思考。

transcript.text: I think about some of the students who took advantage of their opportunities in a university. One of the stories I always like to tell is of a freshman seminar that I had a chance to teach at Harvard when I was president of the university.
transcript.translation: 我会想起一些充分利用了大学机会的学生。我最爱讲的一个故事，是关于我担任哈佛大学校长时有幸教授的一个新生研讨班。

transcript.text: I taught a seminar on globalization and I assigned a reading that I had written about global capital flows. And as I did each week, I asked one of the students to introduce the readings.
transcript.translation: 我教的是一门关于全球化的研讨课，我布置了一篇自己撰写的、关于全球资本流动的阅读材料。和每周一样，我请一位学生来介绍这些阅读材料。

transcript.text: And this young man in October of his freshman year said something like the following. The reading by President Summers on the flow of capital across countries, it was kind of interesting, but the data did not come close to supporting the conclusions.
transcript.translation: 这个年轻人在他大一的十月份说了大致如下的话：萨默斯校长这篇关于跨国资本流动的阅读材料，还算有点意思，但数据远远不足以支撑文中的结论。

transcript.text: And I thought to myself, what a fantastic thing this was. How could somebody who had been there for five weeks tell the person who had the title president that he didn't really know what he was talking about? And it was a special moment.
transcript.translation: 我心想，这真是太棒了。一个才来了五个星期的人，怎么能对一位顶着校长头衔的人说，他其实并不懂自己在讲什么呢？那真是一个特别的时刻。

transcript.text: Now, I don't want to be misunderstood. I explained to my student that I actually thought he was rather more confused than I was. And I argued back.
transcript.translation: 不过，我不想被误解。我向那位学生解释说，我其实觉得他比我更糊涂，于是我也反驳了回去。

transcript.text: But what was really important about that was the universities stand out as places that really are about the authority of ideas. You see it in faculty members who are pleased when their students make a discovery that undermines a cherished theory that they had put forward.
transcript.translation: 但真正重要的是，大学之所以与众不同，正在于它们是崇尚思想权威的地方。你可以在教师身上看到这一点：当学生作出某个发现、推翻了他们曾经珍视并提出的理论时，他们反而感到高兴。

transcript.text: I think of another student I had who came to me one evening, walked into my office and said that I had written a pretty good paper, but that it had five important mistakes and that he wanted a job.
transcript.translation: 我还想起另一位学生，他一天傍晚来找我，走进我的办公室说，我写了一篇相当不错的论文，但里面有五个重要的错误，而且他想要一份工作。

transcript.text: You could debate whether they actually were mistakes, but you couldn't debate that young man's hunger to learn. You could not debate that that young man was someone who wanted to make a difference in economics.
transcript.translation: 你可以争论那些到底算不算错误，但你无法否认那个年轻人对学习的渴望。你无法否认那个年轻人是一个想要在经济学领域有所建树的人。

transcript.text: And he is today a professor of economics, and his works are more cited as an economist than any other economist in the world.
transcript.translation: 如今他已是一位经济学教授，作为经济学家，他的著作被引用的次数超过了世界上任何其他经济学家。

questions.analysis: 录音开头说话人明确指出来大学的目的：'You are here to understand thinking better and to think better yourself.'（你们来这里是为了更好地理解思考、让自己思考得更好），强调大学提升学生的思考能力，故选 B。A 文中只说这是难得的机会，并未说只对有天赋者开放；C 说话人恰恰说这种专注思考的机会'不是一生中随时都有的'，与'终身学习'相反；D '培养众多杰出学者'是后文举例的附带结果，并非他对大学本质的概括。

questions.analysis: 说话人通过一名新生当面质疑校长论文的故事，得出结论：'universities stand out as places that really are about the authority of ideas'（大学之所以与众不同，正在于崇尚思想的权威而非头衔的权威），即鼓励不论身份的学术平等与争鸣，故选 A。B 全球化只是研讨课的主题，并非故事要说明的道理；C 恰好相反，故事强调的是思想的权威而非校长的权威；D 文中并未谈及保护学生权利。

options.label: B

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.text: His potential for leadership.

questions.analysis: 说话人评价那个指出他论文五处错误的学生时说：'you couldn't debate that young man's hunger to learn'（你无法否认那个年轻人对学习的渴望），thirst for knowledge 正是 hunger to learn 的同义改写，故选 A。B 学生虽提到'wanted a job'，但说话人看重的是其求知欲而非找工作的急切；C 学生质疑权威是出于求知而非'蔑视'权威；D 文中提到他后来成为引用率最高的经济学家，体现学术成就而非'领导潜质'。

transcript.text: Recording 2.
transcript.translation: 录音二。

transcript.text: Psychological research shows we consistently underestimate our mental powers.
transcript.translation: 心理学研究表明，我们总是一贯地低估自己的智力。

transcript.text: If you think this does not apply to you, then here is a simple test to show you are wrong.
transcript.translation: 如果你认为这不适用于你，那么这里有一个简单的测试可以证明你是错的。

transcript.text: Write down the names of all the American states you can remember.
transcript.translation: 写下你所能记住的所有美国州名。

transcript.text: Put the list away and then set yourself the same task a week later.
transcript.translation: 把这份清单收起来，一周后再让自己做同样的任务。

transcript.text: Provided you have not cheated by consulting an atlas, you will notice something rather surprising.
transcript.translation: 只要你没有靠查阅地图册作弊，你就会注意到一些相当令人惊讶的现象。

transcript.text: The two lists will contain roughly the same number of states, but they will not be identical.
transcript.translation: 这两份清单所含的州数大致相同，但它们并不完全一样。

transcript.text: Some names will have slipped away, but others will have replaced them.
transcript.translation: 有些名字会消失，但另一些名字会取而代之。

transcript.text: This suggests that somewhere in your mind you may well have a record of virtually every state.
transcript.translation: 这表明，在你脑海的某个地方，你很可能记录着几乎每一个州。

transcript.text: So it is not really your memory letting you down, just your ability to retrieve information from it.
transcript.translation: 所以真正让你失望的并不是你的记忆力，而只是你从记忆中提取信息的能力。

transcript.text: We would remember a lot more if we had more confidence in our memories and knew how to use them properly.
transcript.translation: 如果我们对自己的记忆更有信心，并且懂得如何正确地使用它们，我们就能记住更多东西。

transcript.text: One useful tip is that things are more likely to be remembered if you are in exactly the same state and place as you were when you learned them.
transcript.translation: 一个有用的窍门是：如果你处于与学习时完全相同的状态和地点，那么事物就更容易被记住。

transcript.text: So if you are a student who always reviews over black coffee, perhaps it would be sensible to prime yourself with a cup before the exam.
transcript.translation: 所以如果你是一个总是边喝黑咖啡边复习的学生，也许在考试前先给自己来上一杯是明智的做法。

transcript.text: If possible, you should also try to learn information in the room where it is going to be tested.
transcript.translation: 如果可能的话，你还应该尽量在将要进行考试的房间里学习相关信息。

transcript.text: When you learn is also important.
transcript.translation: 你在什么时候学习也很重要。

transcript.text: Lots of people swear they can absorb new information more efficiently at some times of the day than at others.
transcript.translation: 很多人坚信，他们在一天中的某些时段比其他时段能更高效地吸收新信息。

transcript.text: Research shows this is not just imagination.
transcript.translation: 研究表明，这并非只是想象。

transcript.text: There is a biological rhythm for learning.
transcript.translation: 学习存在着一种生物节律。

transcript.text: Though it affects different people in different ways, for most of us the best plan is to take in new information in the morning and then try to consolidate it into memory during the afternoon.
transcript.translation: 虽然它对不同的人有不同的影响，但对我们大多数人来说，最好的安排是上午吸收新信息，然后在下午努力把它巩固进记忆中。

transcript.text: But this does not apply to everyone, so it is essential to establish your own rhythm.
transcript.translation: 但这并不适用于每个人，所以确立你自己的节律至关重要。

transcript.text: You can do this by learning a set number of lines of poetry at different times of the day and seeing when most lines stick.
transcript.translation: 你可以通过在一天的不同时段背诵固定数量的诗句，并看看在什么时候记住的诗句最多来做到这一点。

transcript.text: When you have done this, try to organize your life so that the time set aside for learning coincides with the time when your memory is at its best.
transcript.translation: 做完这件事后，尽量安排好你的生活，让留给学习的时间正好与你记忆力最佳的时间相吻合。

transcript.text: Avoid learning marathons. They do not make the best use of your mind.
transcript.translation: 避免马拉松式的学习。它们并不能最好地利用你的大脑。

transcript.text: Take plenty of breaks because they offer a double bonus.
transcript.translation: 多多休息，因为休息能带来双重好处。

transcript.text: The time off gives your mind a chance to do some preliminary consolidation and it also gives a memory boost to the learning.
transcript.translation: 休息时间让你的大脑有机会做一些初步的巩固，同时也对学习起到增强记忆的作用。

transcript.text: Hello. Today I am going to talk about poverty.
transcript.translation: 大家好。今天我要谈谈贫困这个话题。

transcript.text: Poverty has become a critical issue in today's world. It concerns not only us sociologists but also economists, politicians and business people.
transcript.translation: 贫困已成为当今世界一个至关重要的问题。它不仅关系到我们社会学家，也关系到经济学家、政治家和商人。

transcript.text: Poverty has been understood in many different ways. One useful way is to distinguish between three degrees of poverty: extreme poverty, moderate poverty and relative poverty.
transcript.translation: 人们以多种不同的方式理解贫困。一种有用的方式是把贫困区分为三种程度：极端贫困、中度贫困和相对贫困。

transcript.text: The first type of poverty is extreme poverty. It is also called absolute poverty.
transcript.translation: 第一种贫困是极端贫困。它也被称为绝对贫困。

transcript.text: In extreme poverty, households cannot meet basic needs for survival. People are chronically hungry. They are unable to access safe drinking water, let alone health care. They cannot afford education for their children.
transcript.translation: 在极端贫困中，家庭无法满足基本的生存需求。人们长期处于饥饿状态。他们无法获得安全的饮用水，更不用说医疗了。他们负担不起子女的教育。

transcript.text: In short, people who live in extreme poverty do not have even the minimum resources to support themselves and their families.
transcript.translation: 简而言之，生活在极端贫困中的人们甚至连维持自己和家人生计所需的最低限度资源都没有。

transcript.text: Where does extreme poverty occur? Well, you can find it only in developing countries.
transcript.translation: 极端贫困发生在哪里呢？嗯，你只能在发展中国家找到它。

transcript.text: Well, what about moderate poverty? Unlike extreme poverty, moderate poverty generally refers to conditions of life in which basic needs are met but barely.
transcript.translation: 那么中度贫困又如何呢？与极端贫困不同，中度贫困通常指的是基本需求得到满足、但仅仅勉强满足的生活状况。

transcript.text: People living in moderate poverty have the resources to keep themselves alive, but only at a very basic level.
transcript.translation: 生活在中度贫困中的人们拥有维持生命的资源，但仅仅处于非常基本的水平。

transcript.text: For example, they may have access to drinking water but not clean, safe drinking water. They may have a home to shelter themselves, but it does not have power supply, a telephone or plumbing.
transcript.translation: 例如，他们可能有饮用水，但不是干净、安全的饮用水。他们可能有遮风挡雨的住所，但没有电力供应、电话或管道设施。

transcript.text: The third kind of poverty is relative poverty. Relative poverty is generally considered to be a household income level which is below a given proportion of average family income.
transcript.translation: 第三种贫困是相对贫困。相对贫困通常被认为是低于平均家庭收入某一特定比例的家庭收入水平。

transcript.text: The relatively poor live in high-income countries, but they do not have a high income themselves.
transcript.translation: 相对贫困者生活在高收入国家，但他们本身收入并不高。

transcript.text: The method of calculating the poverty line is different from country to country, but we can say that basically a family living in relative poverty has less than a certain percentage of the average family income.
transcript.translation: 计算贫困线的方法因国家而异，但我们可以说，生活在相对贫困中的家庭基本上其收入低于平均家庭收入的某一百分比。

transcript.text: For example, in the United States, a family can be considered poor if their income is less than 50% of the national average family income.
transcript.translation: 例如，在美国，如果一个家庭的收入低于全国平均家庭收入的 50%，就可以被认为是贫困的。

transcript.text: They can meet their basic needs, but they lack access to cultural goods, entertainment and recreation. They also do not have access to quality health care or other prerequisites for upward social mobility.
transcript.translation: 他们能满足基本需求，但缺乏获得文化产品、娱乐和休闲的途径。他们也无法获得优质的医疗服务或其他向上社会流动的必要条件。

transcript.text: Well, I have briefly explained to you how poverty can be distinguished as extreme poverty, moderate poverty and relative poverty.
transcript.translation: 好了，我已经向你们简要解释了如何将贫困区分为极端贫困、中度贫困和相对贫困。

transcript.text: We should keep these distinctions in mind when we research people's living conditions, either in the developing or the developed world.
transcript.translation: 当我们研究人们的生活状况时，无论是在发展中世界还是发达世界，都应该牢记这些区别。

New research says that those who can't seem to keep their inner monologues (独白) in are actually more likely to stay on task, remain __26__ better and show improved perception capabilities. Not bad, really, for some extra muttering.
paragraphs.translation: 让我们都停止评判那些自言自语的人。新研究表明，那些似乎无法控制内心独白（独白）的人实际上更可能专注于任务、保持更好的专注力，并表现出改善的感知能力。对于一些额外的嘀咕来说，这真的不错。

paragraphs.text: According to a series of experiments published in the Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology by professors Gary Lupyan and Daniel Swignley, the act of using verbal clues to __27__ mental pictures helps people function quicker.
paragraphs.translation: 根据Gary Lupyan和Daniel Swignley教授在《实验心理学季刊》上发表的一系列实验，使用语言线索来触发心理图像的行为有助于人们更快地运作。

paragraphs.text: In one experiment, they showed pictures of various objects to twenty __28__; and asked them to find just one of those, a banana. Half were __29__ to repeat out loud what they were looking for and the other half kept their lips __30__ Those who talked to themselves found the banana slightly faster than those who didn't, the researchers say. In other experiments, Lupyan and Swignley found that __31__ the name of a common product when on the hunt for it helped quicken someone's pace, but talking about uncommon items showed no advantage and slowed you down.
paragraphs.translation: 在一个实验中，他们向二十名志愿者展示了各种物体的图片；并要求他们找到其中一个，香蕉。一半被指示大声重复他们在找什么，另一半则保持沉默。研究人员说，那些自言自语的人找到香蕉的速度比不自言自语的人稍快。在其他实验中，Lupyan和Swignley发现，在寻找常见产品时说出其名称有助于加快某人的步伐，但谈论不常见的物品则没有优势，反而会减慢你的速度。

paragraphs.text: Common research has long held that talking themselves through a task helps children learn, although doing so when you've __32__ matured is not a great sign of __33__ The two professors hope to refute that idea, __34__ that just as when kids walk themselves through a process, adults can benefit from using language not just to communicate, but also to help "augment thinking".
paragraphs.translation: 长期以来，普遍研究认为，通过自言自语来完成任务有助于儿童学习，尽管在成熟后这样做并不是傲慢的一个好迹象。这两位教授希望反驳这一观点，声称就像孩子们通过自言自语来完成一个过程一样，成年人也可以从使用语言中受益，不仅是为了交流，还可以帮助“增强思维”。

paragraphs.text: Of course, you are still encouraged to keep the talking at library tones and, whatever you do, keep the information you share simple, like a grocery list. At any __35__, there's still such a thing as too much information.

questionGroups.title: Rich Children and Poor Ones Are Raised Very Differently

material.title: Rich Children and Poor Ones Are Raised Very Differently

paragraphs.text: The lives of children from rich and poor American families look more different than ever before.
paragraphs.translation: 来自富裕和贫困美国家庭的孩子们的生活看起来比以往任何时候都更加不同。

paragraphs.text: Well-off families are ruled by calendars, with children enrolled in ballet, soccer and after-school programs, according to a new Pew Research Center survey. There are usually two parents, who spend a lot of time reading to children and worrying about their anxiety levels and hectic schedules.
paragraphs.translation: 根据皮尤研究中心的一项新调查，富裕家庭的日程安排得很满，孩子们参加芭蕾舞、足球和课外项目。通常有两个家长，他们花很多时间给孩子读书，并担心他们的焦虑水平和忙碌的日程。

paragraphs.text: In poor families, meanwhile, children tend to spend their time at home or with extended family. They are more likely to grow up in neighborhoods that their parents say aren't great for raising children, and their parents worry about them getting shot, beaten up or in trouble with the law.
paragraphs.translation: 与此同时，在贫困家庭中，孩子们往往待在家里或与大家庭在一起。他们更可能成长在父母认为不适合抚养孩子的社区，父母担心他们被枪击、殴打或惹上法律麻烦。

paragraphs.text: The class differences in child rearing are growing — a symptom of widening inequality with far- reaching consequences. Different upbringings set children on different paths and can deepen socioeconomic divisions, especially because education is strongly linked to earnings. Children grow up learning the skills to succeed in their socioeconomic stratum (阶层), but not necessarily others.
paragraphs.translation: 育儿中的阶级差异正在扩大——这是不平等加剧的一个症状，具有深远的影响。不同的成长经历将孩子们引向不同的道路，并可能加深社会经济分化，尤其是因为教育与收入密切相关。孩子们在成长过程中学习在其社会经济阶层（阶层）中取得成功的技能，但不一定适用于其他阶层。

paragraphs.text: "Early childhood experiences can be very consequential for children's long-term social, emotional and cognitive development," said Sean Reardon, professor of poverty and inequality in education at Stanford University. "And because those influence educational success and later earnings, early childhood experiences cast a lifelong shadow." The cycle continues: Poor parents have less time and fewer resources to invest in their children, which can leave children less prepared for school and work, which leads to lower earnings.
paragraphs.translation: “早期童年经历对孩子的长期社交、情感和认知发展非常重要，”斯坦福大学教育贫困与不平等教授Sean Reardon说。“而且，因为这些经历影响教育成功和后续收入，早期童年经历会投下终身阴影。”这个循环持续：贫困父母有更少的时间和资源投资于孩子，这可能导致孩子对学校和工作准备不足，从而导致较低的收入。

paragraphs.text: American parents want similar things for their children, the Pew report and past research have found: for them to be healthy and happy, honest and ethical, caring and compassionate. There is no best parenting style or philosophy, researchers say, and across income groups, 92% of parents say they are doing a good job at raising their children. Yet they are doing it quite differently. Middle-class and higher-income parents see their children as projects in need of careful cultivation, says Annette Lareau, whose groundbreaking research on the topic was published in her book Unequal Childhoods: Class, Race and Family Life. They try to develop their skills through close supervision and organized activities, and teach children to question authority figures and navigate elite institutions.
paragraphs.translation: 皮尤报告和过去的研究发现，美国父母为孩子想要相似的东西：他们健康快乐、诚实有道德、关心有同情心。研究人员说，没有最好的育儿风格或理念，在收入群体中，92%的父母认为他们在抚养孩子方面做得很好。然而，他们的方式截然不同。中产阶级和较高收入的父母将孩子视为需要精心培养的项目，Annette Lareau说，她关于这个话题的开创性研究发表在她的书《不平等的童年：阶级、种族和家庭生活》中。他们试图通过密切监督和有组织的活动来发展孩子的技能，并教导孩子质疑权威人物和应对精英机构。

paragraphs.text: Working-class parents, meanwhile, believe their children will naturally thrive, and give them far greater independence and time for free play. They are taught to be compliant and respectful to adults. There are benefits to both approaches. Working-class children are happier, more independent, complain less and are closer to family members, Ms. Lareau found. Higher-income children are more likely to declare boredom and expect their parents to solve their problems. Yet later on, the more affluent children end up in college and on the way to the middle class, while working-class children tend to struggle. Children from higher-income families are likely to have the skills to navigate bureaucracies and succeed in schools and workplaces, Ms. Lareau said.
paragraphs.translation: 与此同时，工薪阶层的父母相信他们的孩子会自然茁壮成长，并给予他们更大的独立性和自由玩耍的时间。他们被教导要顺从并尊重成年人。这两种方法都有好处。Lareau女士发现，工薪阶层的孩子更快乐、更独立、抱怨更少、更亲近家人。较高收入的孩子更可能表示无聊并期望父母解决问题。然而，后来，更富裕的孩子进入大学并走上中产阶级之路，而工薪阶层的孩子往往挣扎。来自较高收入家庭的孩子可能具备应对官僚体系并在学校和工作场所取得成功的技能，Lareau女士说。

paragraphs.text: "Do all parents want the most success for their children? Absolutely," she said. "Do some strategies give children more advantages than others in institutions? Probably they do. Will parents be damaging children if they have one fewer organized activity? No, I really doubt it."
paragraphs.translation: “所有父母都希望孩子取得最大成功吗？绝对是的，”她说。“一些策略在机构中给孩子带来更多优势吗？可能确实如此。如果父母少组织一个活动，会损害孩子吗？不，我非常怀疑。”

paragraphs.text: Social scientists say the differences arise in part because low-income parents have less money to spend on music class or preschool, and less flexible schedules to take children to museums or attend school events. Extracurricular activities reflect the differences in child rearing in the Pew survey, which was of a nationally representative sample of 1,807 parents. Of families earning more that $75,000 a year, 84% say their children have participated in organized sports over the past year, 64% have done volunteer work and 62% have taken lessons in music, dance or art. Of families earning less than $30,000, 59% of children have done sports, 37% have volunteered and 41% have taken arts classes.
paragraphs.translation: 社会科学家说，这些差异部分是因为低收入父母没有太多钱花在音乐课或学前班上，也没有灵活的时间带孩子去博物馆或参加学校活动。皮尤调查中的课外活动反映了育儿差异，该调查基于一个全国代表性的1807名父母样本。在年收入超过75,000美元的家庭中，84%表示他们的孩子在过去一年参加了有组织的体育运动，64%做过志愿服务，62%上过音乐、舞蹈或艺术课程。在年收入低于30,000美元的家庭中，59%的孩子参加过体育运动，37%做过志愿服务，41%上过艺术课。

paragraphs.text: Especially in affluent families, children start young. Nearly half of high-earning, college-graduate parents enrolled their children in arts classes before they were 5, compared with one-fifth of low-income, less-educated parents. Nonetheless, 20% of well-off parents say their children's schedules are too hectic, compared with 8% of poorer parents.
paragraphs.translation: 特别是在富裕家庭，孩子们开始得早。近一半的高收入、大学毕业的父母在孩子5岁前就让他们参加艺术课，而低收入、教育程度较低的父母中只有五分之一。尽管如此，20%的富裕父母表示孩子的日程太忙碌，而较贫困的父母中只有8%。

paragraphs.text: Another example is reading aloud, which studies have shown gives children bigger vocabularies and better reading comprehension in school. 71% of parents with a college degree say they do it every day, compared with 33% of those with a high school diploma or less. White parents are more likely than others to read to their children daily, as are married parents. Most affluent parents enroll their children in preschool or day care, while low-income parents are more likely to depend on family members. Discipline techniques vary by education level: 8% of those with a postgraduate degree say they often beat their children, compared with 22% of those with a high school degree or less.
paragraphs.translation: 另一个例子是大声朗读，研究表明这能给孩子更大的词汇量和更好的学校阅读理解能力。71%的大学学历父母表示他们每天这样做，而高中或更低学历的父母中只有33%。白人父母比其他人更可能每天给孩子读书，已婚父母也是如此。大多数富裕父母让孩子上幼儿园或日托，而低收入父母更可能依赖家庭成员。纪律技巧因教育水平而异：8%的研究生学历父母表示他们经常打孩子，而高中或更低学历的父母中有22%。

paragraphs.text: The survey also probed attitudes and anxieties. Interestingly, parents' attitudes toward education do not seem to reflect their own educational background as much as a belief in the importance of education for upward mobility. Most American parents say they are not concerned about their children's grades as long as they work hard. But 50% of poor parents say it is extremely important to them that their children earn a college degree, compared with 39% of wealthier parents.
paragraphs.translation: 调查还探讨了态度和焦虑。有趣的是，父母对教育的态度似乎更多地反映了他们对教育对向上流动重要性的信念，而不是他们自己的教育背景。大多数美国父母表示，只要孩子努力学习，他们并不关心成绩。但50%的贫困父母表示，孩子获得大学学位对他们极其重要，而较富裕的父母中有39%。

paragraphs.text: Less-educated parents, and poorer and black and Latino parents are more likely to believe that there is no such thing as too much involvement in a child's education. Parents who are white, wealthy or college-educated say too much involvement can be bad. Parental anxieties reflect their circumstances. High-earning parents are much more likely to say they live in a good neighborhood for raising children. While bullying is parents' greatest concern over all, nearly half of low-income parents worry their child will get shot, compared with one-fifth of high-income parents. They are more worried about their children being depressed or anxious.
paragraphs.translation: 教育程度较低的父母，以及较贫困、黑人和拉丁裔父母更可能认为，在孩子的教育中没有过度参与这回事。白人、富裕或大学毕业的父母说过度参与可能有害。父母的焦虑反映了他们的处境。高收入父母更可能表示他们住在适合抚养孩子的好社区。虽然欺凌是父母总体上最大的担忧，但近一半的低收入父母担心孩子被枪击，而高收入父母中只有五分之一。他们更担心孩子抑郁或焦虑。

paragraphs.text: In the Pew survey, middle-class families earning between $30,000 and $75,000 a year fell right between working-class and high-earning parents on issues like the quality of their neighborhood for raising children, participation in extracurricular activities and involvement in their children's education.
paragraphs.translation: 在皮尤调查中，年收入在30,000到75,000美元之间的中产阶级家庭，在诸如社区质量、课外活动参与和孩子教育参与等问题上，正好介于工薪阶层和高收入父母之间。

paragraphs.text: Children were not always raised so differently. The achievement gap between children from high- and low-income families is 30-40% larger among children born in 2001 than those born 25 years earlier, according to Mr. Reardon's research. People used to live near people of different income levels; neighborhoods are now more segregated by income. More than a quarter of children live in single parent households — a historic high, according to Pew — and these children are three times as likely to live in poverty as those who live with married parents. Meanwhile, growing income inequality has coincided with the increasing importance of a college degree for earning a middle-class wage.
paragraphs.translation: 孩子们并非总是以如此不同的方式被抚养。根据Reardon先生的研究，2001年出生的孩子中，高低收入家庭之间的成就差距比25年前出生的孩子大30-40%。过去人们住在不同收入水平的人附近；现在社区更按收入隔离。超过四分之一的孩子生活在单亲家庭——根据皮尤的数据，这是历史新高——这些孩子生活在贫困中的可能性是与已婚父母生活的孩子的三倍。与此同时，收入不平等加剧的同时，大学学位对于赚取中产阶级工资的重要性也在增加。

paragraphs.text: Yet there are recent signs that the gap could be starting to shrink. In the past decade, even as income inequality has grown, some of the socioeconomic differences in parenting, like reading to children and going to libraries, have narrowed.
paragraphs.translation: 然而，最近有迹象表明，这个差距可能开始缩小。在过去十年中，尽管收入不平等加剧，但育儿中的一些社会经济差异，如给孩子读书和去图书馆，已经缩小。

paragraphs.text: Public policies aimed at young children have helped, including public preschool programs and reading initiatives. Addressing differences in the earliest years, it seems, could reduce inequality in the next generation.
paragraphs.translation: 针对幼儿的公共政策有所帮助，包括公共学前班项目和阅读倡议。解决最早年份的差异，似乎可以减少下一代的不平等。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: Tennessee's technical and community colleges will not outsource (外包) management of their facilities to a private company, a decision one leader said was bolstered by an analysis of spending at each campus.
paragraphs.translation: 田纳西州的技术和社区学院不会将其设施管理外包给一家私营公司，一位领导人表示，这一决定得到了对每个校园支出分析的支撑。

paragraphs.text: In an email sent Monday to college presidents in the Tennessee Board of Regents system, outgoing Chancellor John Morgan said an internal analysis showed that each campus' spending on facilities management fell well below the industry standards identified by the state. Morgan said those findings — which included data from the system's 13 community colleges, 27 technical colleges and six universities — were part of the decision not to move forward with Governor Bill Haslam's proposal to privatize management of state buildings in an effort to save money.
paragraphs.translation: 在周一发给田纳西州校董会系统学院校长的电子邮件中，即将离任的校长约翰·摩根表示，内部分析显示，每个校园在设施管理上的支出远低于该州确定的行业标准。摩根说，这些发现——包括该系统13所社区学院、27所技术学院和6所大学的数据——是决定不推进州长比尔·哈斯拉姆为节省资金而提议将州立建筑管理私有化的一部分。

paragraphs.text: "While these numbers are still being validated by the state, we feel any adjustments they might suggest will be immaterial," Morgan wrote to the presidents. "System institutions are operating very efficiently based on this analysis, raising the question of the value of pursuing a broad scale outsourcing initiative."
paragraphs.translation: “虽然这些数字仍在由州政府验证，但我们认为他们可能提出的任何调整都将是无关紧要的，”摩根在写给校长的信中说道。“基于这一分析，系统机构运营非常高效，这引发了对推行大规模外包计划价值的疑问。”

paragraphs.text: Workers' advocates have criticized Haslam's plan, saying it would mean some campus workers would lose their jobs or benefits. Haslam has said colleges would be free to opt in or out of the outsourcing plan, which has not been finalized.
paragraphs.translation: 工人倡导者批评了哈斯拉姆的计划，称这将意味着一些校园工人将失去工作或福利。哈斯拉姆曾表示，学院可以自由选择加入或退出外包计划，该计划尚未最终确定。

paragraphs.text: Morgan notified the Haslam administration of his decision to opt out in a letter sent last week. That letter, which includes several concerns Morgan has with the plan, was originally obtained by The Commercial Appeal in Memphis.
paragraphs.translation: 摩根在上周发送的一封信中通知了哈斯拉姆政府他决定退出的决定。这封信包含了摩根对该计划的几点担忧，最初由孟菲斯的《商业呼声报》获得。

paragraphs.text: In an email statement from the state's Office of Customer Focused Government, which is examining the possibility of outsourcing, spokeswoman Michelle R. Martin said officials were still working to analyze the data from the Board of Regents. Data on management expenses at the college system and in other state departments will be part of a "business justification" the state will use as officials deliberate the specifics of an outsourcing plan.
paragraphs.translation: 在州客户服务政府办公室的一份电子邮件声明中，该办公室正在审查外包的可能性，发言人米歇尔·R·马丁表示，官员们仍在努力分析来自校董会的数据。学院系统和其他州部门的管理费用数据将成为州政府官员审议外包计划细节时使用的“商业理由”的一部分。

paragraphs.text: "The state's facilities management project team is still in the process of developing its business justification and expects to have that completed and available to the public at the end of February," Martin said. "At this time there is nothing to take action on since the analysis has yet to be completed."
paragraphs.translation: “州设施管理项目团队仍在制定其商业理由的过程中，预计将在二月底完成并向公众提供，”马丁说。“目前没有需要采取行动的事项，因为分析尚未完成。”

paragraphs.text: Morgan's comments on outsourcing mark the second time this month that he has come out against one of Haslam's plans for higher education in Tennessee. Morgan said last week that he would retire at the end of January because of the governor's proposal to split off six universities of the Board of Regents system and create separate governing boards for each of them. In his resignation letter, Morgan called the reorganization "unworkable."
paragraphs.translation: 摩根关于外包的评论标志着他本月第二次公开反对哈斯拉姆在田纳西州高等教育方面的计划之一。摩根上周表示，他将在一月底退休，原因是州长提议将校董会系统的六所大学分离出来，并为每所大学创建独立的治理委员会。在辞职信中，摩根称重组“不可行”。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: Beginning in the late sixteenth century, it became fashionable for young aristocrats to visit Paris, Venice, Florence, and above all, Rome, as the culmination (终极) of their classical education. Thus was born the idea of the Grand Tour, a practice which introduced Englishmen, Germans, Scandinavians, and also Americans to the art and culture of France and Italy for the next 300 years. Travel was arduous and costly throughout the period, possible only for a privileged class — the same that produced gentlemen scientists, authors, antique experts, and patrons of the arts.
paragraphs.translation: 从十六世纪末开始，年轻贵族访问巴黎、威尼斯、佛罗伦萨，尤其是罗马，作为其古典教育的终极目标，成为一种时尚。由此诞生了“大旅行”的概念，这一实践在接下来的300年中向英国人、德国人、斯堪的纳维亚人以及美国人介绍了法国和意大利的艺术与文化。整个时期的旅行既艰辛又昂贵，只可能由特权阶层承担——正是这个阶层产生了绅士科学家、作家、古董专家和艺术赞助人。

paragraphs.text: The Grand Tourist was typically a young man with a thorough grounding in Greek and Latin literature as well as some leisure time, some means, and some interest in art. The German traveler Johann Winckelmann pioneered the field of art history with his comprehensive study of Greek and Roman sculpture; he was portrayed by his friend Anton Raphael Mengs at the beginning of his long residence in Rome. Most Grand Tourists, however, stayed for briefer periods and set out with less scholarly intentions, accompanied by a teacher or guardian, and expected to return home with souvenirs of their travels as well as an understanding of art and architecture formed by exposure to great masterpieces.
paragraphs.translation: 大旅行者通常是一位在希腊和拉丁文学方面有扎实基础的年轻男子，同时拥有一定的闲暇时间、财力和对艺术的兴趣。德国旅行家约翰·温克尔曼通过对希腊和罗马雕塑的全面研究开创了艺术史领域；他在长期居住罗马的初期，由其朋友安东·拉斐尔·门斯描绘了肖像。然而，大多数大旅行者停留时间较短，出发时学术意图较少，由教师或监护人陪同，并期望在回国时带回旅行的纪念品，以及通过接触伟大杰作形成的对艺术和建筑的理解。

paragraphs.text: London was a frequent starting point for Grand Tourists, and Paris a compulsory destination; many traveled to the Netherlands, some to Switzerland and Germany, and a very few adventurers to Spain, Greece, or Turkey. The essential place to visit, however, was Italy. The British traveler Charles Thompson spoke for many Grand Tourists when in 1744 he described himself as "being impatiently desirous of viewing a country so famous in history, a country which once gave laws to the world, and which is at present the greatest school of music and painting, contains the noblest productions of sculpture and architecture, and is filled with cabinets of rarities, and collections of all kinds of historical relics." Within Italy, the great focus was Rome, whose ancient ruins and more recent achievements were shown to every Grand Tourist. Panini's Ancient Rome and Modern Rome represent the sights most prized, including celebrated Greco-Roman statues and views of famous ruins, fountains, and churches. Since there were few museums anywhere in Europe before the close of the eighteenth century, Grand Tourists often saw paintings and sculptures by gaining admission to private collections, and many were eager to acquire examples of Greco-Roman and Italian art for their own collections. In England, where architecture was increasingly seen as an aristocratic pursuit, noblemen often applied what they learned from the villas of Palladio in the Veneto and the evocative (唤起回忆的) ruins of Rome to their own country houses and gardens.
paragraphs.translation: 伦敦是大旅行者常见的起点，巴黎是必去的目的地；许多人前往荷兰，一些人前往瑞士和德国，极少数冒险者前往西班牙、希腊或土耳其。然而，最重要的地方是意大利。英国旅行家查尔斯·汤普森在1744年代表许多大旅行者表达了心声，他描述自己“急切渴望亲眼目睹这个在历史上如此著名的国家，这个曾经为世界制定法律的国家，目前是音乐和绘画的最高学府，拥有最高贵的雕塑和建筑作品，并且遍布珍品柜和各种历史文物收藏。”在意大利，主要焦点是罗马，其古代遗迹和近期成就被展示给每一位大旅行者。帕尼尼的《古代罗马》和《现代罗马》代表了最受珍视的景观，包括著名的希腊罗马雕像以及著名遗迹、喷泉和教堂的景色。由于十八世纪末之前欧洲各地博物馆稀少，大旅行者常常通过进入私人收藏来观赏绘画和雕塑，许多人渴望为自己的收藏获取希腊罗马和意大利艺术的范例。在英国，建筑日益被视为贵族追求，贵族们经常将他们在威尼托的帕拉第奥别墅和罗马令人唤起回忆的遗迹中学到的东西应用于自己的乡村住宅和花园。

questions.questionText: What is said about the Grand Tour?

options.label: A
options.text: It was fashionable among young people of the time.

options.label: B
options.text: It was unaffordable for ordinary people.

options.label: C
options.text: It produced some famous European artists.

options.label: D
options.text: It made a compulsory part of college education.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章第二段提到'Travel was arduous and costly throughout the period, possible only for a privileged class'，说明大旅行对于普通人来说是负担不起的，因此B选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 虽然大旅行在年轻人中流行，但原文强调的是它仅限于特权阶层，所以A选项不全面。
wrongOptions.C: 文章没有提到大旅行产生了著名的欧洲艺术家，所以C选项是无中生有。
wrongOptions.D: 文章中没有提到大旅行是大学教育的必修部分，所以D选项是无中生有。

questions.questionText: What did Grand Tourists have in common?

options.label: A
options.text: They had much geographic knowledge.

options.label: B
options.text: They were courageous and venturesome.

options.label: C
options.text: They were versed in literature and interested in art.

options.label: D
options.text: They had enough travel and outdoor-life experience.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章第二段提到'The Grand Tourist was typically a young man with a thorough grounding in Greek and Latin literature as well as some interest in art'，说明大旅行者通常具有文学基础并对艺术感兴趣，因此C选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 文章没有提到大旅行者具有丰富的地理知识，所以A选项是无中生有。
wrongOptions.B: 虽然有些大旅行者可能具有冒险精神，但文章没有特别强调这一点，所以B选项是过度推断。
wrongOptions.D: 文章没有提到大旅行者具有足够的旅行和户外生活经验，所以D选项是无中生有。

questions.questionText: How did Grand Tourists benefit from their travel?

options.label: A
options.text: They found inspiration in the world's greatest masterpieces.

options.label: B
options.text: They got a better understanding of early human civilization.

options.label: C
options.text: They developed an interest in the origin of modern art forms.

options.label: D
options.text: They gained some knowledge of classical art and architecture.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章第二段提到'expected to return home with souvenirs of their travels as well as an understanding of art and architecture formed by exposure to great masterpieces'，说明大旅行者通过接触伟大的艺术作品，获得了对古典艺术和建筑的了解，因此D选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 虽然大旅行者可能在艺术作品中找到灵感，但文章没有明确提到这一点，所以A选项是过度推断。
wrongOptions.B: 文章没有提到大旅行者对早期人类文明有了更好的理解，所以B选项是无中生有。
wrongOptions.C: 文章没有提到大旅行者对现代艺术形式的起源产生了兴趣，所以C选项是无中生有。

questions.questionText: Why did many Grand Tourists visit the private collections?

options.label: A
options.text: They could buy unique souvenirs there to take back home.

options.label: B
options.text: Europe hardly had any museums before the 19th century.

options.label: C
options.text: They found the antiques there more valuable.

options.label: D
options.text: Private collections were of greater variety.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章倒数第二段提到'Since there were few museums anywhere in Europe before the close of the eighteenth century, Grand Tourists often saw paintings and sculptures by gaining admission to private collections'，说明由于18世纪末之前欧洲几乎没有博物馆，大旅行者通过参观私人收藏来观赏绘画和雕塑，因此B选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 虽然大旅行者可能在私人收藏中购买独特的纪念品，但这不是他们参观的主要原因，所以A选项是张冠李戴。
wrongOptions.C: 文章没有提到大旅行者认为私人收藏中的古董更有价值，所以C选项是无中生有。
wrongOptions.D: 文章没有提到私人收藏的种类更丰富，所以D选项是无中生有。

questions.questionText: How did the Grand Tour influence the architecture in England?

options.label: A
options.text: There appeared more and more Roman-style buildings.

options.label: B
options.text: Many aristocrats began to move into Roman-style villas.

options.label: C
options.text: Aristocrats' country houses all had Roman-style gardens.

options.label: D
options.text: Italian architects were hired to design houses and gardens.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章最后一段提到'noble men often applied what they learned from the villas of Palladio in the Veneto and the evocative ruins of Rome to their own country houses and gardens'，说明贵族们将从罗马废墟中学到的知识应用到自己的乡村住宅和花园中，导致出现了越来越多的罗马风格建筑，因此A选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.B: 文章没有提到许多贵族开始搬进罗马风格的别墅，所以B选项是无中生有。
wrongOptions.C: 文章没有提到贵族的乡村住宅都有罗马风格的花园，所以C选项是无中生有。
wrongOptions.D: 文章没有提到雇佣意大利建筑师来设计房屋和花园，所以D选项是无中生有。

questionGroups.sourceText: 宋朝始于 960 年，一直延续到 1279 年。这一时期，中国经济大幅增长，成为世界上最先进的经济体，科学、技术、哲学和数学蓬勃发展。宋代中国是世界历史上首先发行纸币的国家, 宋朝还最早使用火药并发明了活字(movable-type)印刷。人口增长迅速，越来越多的人住进城市，那里有热闹的娱乐场所, 社会生活多种多样, 人们聚集在一起观看和交易珍贵艺术品。宋朝的政府体制在当时也是先进的, 政府官员均通过竞争性考试选拔任用。

answer.modelTranslation: The Song Dynasty began in 960 AD and lasted until 1279 AD. During this period, China's economy grew significantly, becoming one of the world's most advanced economies, with science, technology, philosophy, and mathematics flourishing. China during the Song Dynasty was the first in world history to issue paper currency and was also the earliest to use gunpowder and invent movable-type printing. The population grew rapidly, with more and more people moving into cities, where there were bustling entertainment venues, diverse social life, and people gathered to watch and trade precious artworks. The government system of the Song Dynasty was also advanced for its time, with government officials selected through competitive examinations.
